name: Minervini VCP Stage 2 Breakout
description: LONG ONLY. Mark Minervini's Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP) Stage 2 breakout from Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard (2013). Minervini is a 2x US Investing Champion (1997, 2021) with a documented 1997 return of ~220%. Filters TSX leaders passing the 8-criterion Trend Template — price above rising 50/150/200 MAs, within 25% of 52-week high, at least 30% above 52-week low. Enters pivot breakouts from 3-6 progressively tighter volatility contractions on volume expansion. Documented A+ setup win rate 50-70% with 3:1+ R:R.
screening_prompt: Canadian TSX mid-to-large cap stocks in confirmed Stage 2 uptrends showing Minervini Trend Template alignment price above rising 50 150 and 200 day moving averages within 25 percent of 52 week high at least 30 percent above 52 week low strong relative strength leadership high quality fundamentals improving earnings volatility contraction pattern forming with 3 to 6 pullbacks of decreasing depth and diminishing volume ready for pivot breakout on volume surge
ta_focus: LONG ONLY — do NOT recommend SHORT positions. MINERVINI VCP STAGE 2 BREAKOUT — EXACT RULES from Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard (2013). (1) TREND TEMPLATE (all 8 must be true): (a) Price above 150-day and 200-day MA. (b) 150-day MA above 200-day MA. (c) 200-day MA trending up for at least 1 month. (d) 50-day MA above both 150-day and 200-day MA. (e) Price above 50-day MA. (f) Price at least 30% above 52-week low. (g) Price within 25% of 52-week high. (h) Relative Strength rank in top quartile of market. (2) VCP PATTERN: Identify 3 to 6 progressively tighter pullbacks — each successive contraction must be shallower than the last (e.g. 25% -> 15% -> 8% -> 4%). Volume dries up on each successive contraction, final base < 50% of avg volume. Base duration typically 3 to 65 weeks. (3) PIVOT BREAKOUT ENTRY — CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: Only call BUY after the daily candle CLOSES above the pivot high (top of final tight contraction) on volume >= 1.5x 50-day avg. Before that close, use WATCH with the pivot high as entry_price. Do NOT front-run the breakout. (4) STOP-LOSS: Hard stop at the low of the final contraction (typically 3-7% under entry). Absolute max risk 7-8% per Minervini. (5) POSITION SIZING: 4% max per position, 3-5 concurrent A+ setups. (6) EXIT RULES: Hold as long as price stays above 10-day MA (short-term) or 21-day EMA (position). Sell into strength on 20-25% gain, trail stop under 50-day MA. Time stop 10 days if no follow-through. (7) VOLUME SIGNATURE: Volume DECREASING through the VCP base and EXPANDING sharply on the breakout day — the institutional footprint Minervini calls the 'volume signature'. AVOID: wide-and-loose bases, late-stage bases (4th+ stage), climax tops (parabolic + high volume + wide range).
trading_style: Minervini VCP swing breakout trader, 3-10 day holds targeting Stage 2 pivot breakouts in TSX leaders, LONG ONLY

name: O'Neil CAN SLIM Cup-and-Handle
description: LONG ONLY. William O'Neil's Cup-and-Handle base breakout from How to Make Money in Stocks (1988) and IBD's century-long study of leading stocks. Screens TSX growth leaders in constructive bases with CAN SLIM quality (high ROE, earnings growth, low debt). Enters pivot breakouts on 40%+ volume surge above the handle high. Cup-and-handle documented breakout success ~50-65% when volume confirmation is present.
screening_prompt: TSX growth leaders in cup and handle or flat base patterns near 52 week highs strong quarterly earnings acceleration high return on equity above 15 percent low debt to equity market leaders in sector rotation improving fundamentals recent analyst upgrades constructive base building 7 to 65 weeks long ready for pivot breakout on volume surge
ta_focus: LONG ONLY — do NOT recommend SHORT positions. O'NEIL CAN SLIM CUP-AND-HANDLE — EXACT RULES from How to Make Money in Stocks (1988). (1) BASE STRUCTURE: Cup duration 7 to 65 weeks (most 3-6 months). Cup depth 12-33% ideal, no more than 50%. Cup should be U-shaped and rounded, NOT V-shaped (V = weak base). Left side down gradual, right side up similarly measured. (2) HANDLE: Forms in upper half of cup, drifts DOWN 10-15%, never more than 15%. Duration 1-4 weeks. Volume must dry up in the handle (below 50-day avg). Handle low should sit above the 50-day MA. (3) PIVOT POINT: Handle high + $0.10 = the buy point. (4) CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: Only call BUY after a daily candle CLOSES above the pivot on volume >= 40% above 50-day avg (O'Neil's minimum). 100%+ preferred. Low-volume breakouts fail ~70% of the time. Before that close, use WATCH with the pivot as entry_price. Do NOT chase >5% extended above the pivot. (5) FUNDAMENTAL FILTERS (CAN SLIM): C = Current quarterly EPS growth >= 25%. A = Annual EPS growth >= 25% over 3+ years. Prefer ROE >= 17%. N = New product/service/high. S = Supply-Demand favorable (low float, insider ownership). L = Leader in sector (RS rank top 20%). (6) STOP-LOSS: Fixed 7-8% below pivot (O'Neil's absolute rule). (7) TARGETS: Sell 20-25% partial gain, trail rest with 50-day MA. Bases 1-2 are highest quality; avoid 4th-stage bases. (8) OTHER O'NEIL BASES ACCEPTED: Flat base (5-6 weeks, <15% correction, breakout above prior high), Double bottom (W-shape, second low below first, breakout above middle peak), High-Tight Flag (100-120% run in 4-8 weeks, then 3-5 week flag correcting <25%).
trading_style: CAN SLIM cup-and-handle swing breakout trader, 3-10 day holds targeting growth leaders on volume-confirmed base breakouts, LONG ONLY

name: Darvas Box 52-Week High Breakout
description: LONG ONLY. Nicolas Darvas's box theory from How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960) — the strategy that took him from $36k to $2.25M in 18 months. Screens TSX leaders forming tight rectangular price boxes near 52-week highs, entering on close above the box high with 1.5x+ volume, trailing an ATR-based stop and pyramiding into each new box. Modern backtests report ~55-60% win rate with profit factor ~2.5.
screening_prompt: TSX quality large caps trading within 10 percent of 52 week highs forming tight rectangular consolidation boxes with narrow price range less than 5 percent over 4 to 8 weeks strong prior uptrend leg intact volume drying up during consolidation confirmed sector strength ready to break out to new highs on volume surge institutional accumulation footprint
ta_focus: LONG ONLY — do NOT recommend SHORT positions. DARVAS BOX BREAKOUT — EXACT RULES from How I Made $2,000,000 (1960). (1) BOX DEFINITION: A rectangular consolidation formed after a strong uptrend. Box high = highest close over the last 4 weeks that has NOT been exceeded for 3 consecutive days. Box low = lowest close over the last 4 weeks that has NOT been undercut for 3 consecutive days. Range within the box should be tight, ideally 3-5% high to low. (2) LOCATION FILTER: Only trade boxes forming within 10% of the 52-week high — Darvas only bought stocks making new highs, never mid-range. (3) PRIOR UPTREND: Clean rising trend before the box (EMA 50 > EMA 200 and rising, price above both). (4) CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: Only call BUY after a daily candle CLOSES above the box high on volume >= 1.5x 50-day avg. Before that close, use WATCH with the box high as entry_price. (5) STOP-LOSS: Initial stop just below the box LOW (Darvas's original rule — full box stop). More aggressive: box midpoint. (6) TRAILING STOP: Once a new box forms above the entry box, raise the stop to just below the new box low. Pyramid: add position on each new box breakout. (7) EXIT RULE: Exit on close below the current box low. Mechanical — do NOT second-guess. (8) POSITION SIZING: 3-4% per initial position, pyramiding up to 3 boxes. Max 4 concurrent Darvas boxes to avoid concentration. (9) CONFIRMATION FILTERS: RSI 55-85 (momentum intact but not exhausted), ADX >= 22 (directional strength), Supertrend green, Bollinger Bands showing squeeze THEN expansion on breakout, volume signature — drying up in box then surge on breakout.
trading_style: Darvas Box breakout trader, 3-10 day holds pyramiding into consecutive box breakouts on 52-week-high leaders, LONG ONLY

name: Turtle 20-Day Channel Breakout
description: LONG ONLY. Richard Dennis and Bill Eckhardt's Turtle Trading System 1 (1983-88), documented in Curtis Faith's Way of the Turtle (2007). Classic systematic trend-following: enter long on close above the 20-day high, exit on close below the 10-day low, ATR-based position sizing, hard 2N stop. Skip if last 20-day breakout would have been profitable. Documented win rate ~50-55% with profit factor 2-3 across decades of trend-following studies (Clenow, Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen).
screening_prompt: TSX liquid stocks with sustained uptrend momentum trading near recent multi week highs volatility expanding out of compression institutional accumulation footprint low correlation across positions favoring diversified single name trend followers looking for 20 day price channel breakout candidates with clean rising average true range
ta_focus: LONG ONLY — do NOT recommend SHORT positions. TURTLE SYSTEM 1 (20-day) + SYSTEM 2 (55-day) — EXACT RULES from Way of the Turtle (2007). (1) SYSTEM 1 ENTRY — CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: Only call BUY on daily CLOSE above the 20-day high (highest close of last 20 sessions). Read the 20-day high visually from the daily chart — Chart-Img does NOT render Donchian channels natively, so identify the highest closing price on the chart over the last 20 candles. Before that close, use WATCH with the 20-day high as entry_price. (2) FILTER RULE: Skip the current 20-day breakout signal IF the previous 20-day breakout would have been a winner. Only take breakouts after a losing prior breakout — prevents whipsaws in choppy conditions. (3) SYSTEM 1 EXIT: Exit on close below the 10-day low (lowest close of last 10 sessions). (4) SYSTEM 2 ENTRY: Enter LONG on close above the 55-day high. No filter rule — take every 55-day breakout. (5) SYSTEM 2 EXIT: Exit on close below the 20-day low. (6) POSITION SIZING (N-based, key Turtle innovation): N = 20-day exponential moving average of True Range (ATR-20). Unit size = (1% of account) / (N * Point Value). Each position = 1 Unit. Cap 4 units in a single instrument, 6 units in closely correlated instruments, 12 units total across all trades. (7) HARD STOP-LOSS: 2N below entry (2x ATR-20). Never wider. (8) PYRAMIDING: Add 1 unit each +0.5N above previous entry (so entry, +0.5N, +1.0N, +1.5N max 4 units). Move stop to 2N below MOST RECENT unit as you add. (9) VOLATILITY / TREND CONFIRMATION: Prefer ADX >= 20 (directional), ATR expanding (not compressing), EMA 50 > EMA 200 (structural bull trend), Supertrend green. (10) NO PREDICTION — pure mechanical execution. Discipline > opinion.
trading_style: Turtle-style channel breakout trend follower, 3-10 day System 1 holds with ATR-based sizing and 2N stops, LONG ONLY

name: Pocket Pivot Volume Signature Buy
description: LONG ONLY. Gil Morales & Chris Kacher's pocket pivot from Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple (2010) — an early-entry refinement of CAN SLIM that gets you into leading stocks BEFORE the standard base breakout. A pocket pivot fires when the current up-day's volume exceeds the maximum down-day volume of the last 10 trading days, while the stock is in a constructive base above its 50-day MA. Author backtests show ~60% win rate with tighter stops than standard CAN SLIM entries.
screening_prompt: TSX growth leaders in constructive 3 to 15 week bases above rising 50 day moving average not extended more than 5 percent above 10 day moving average showing early institutional accumulation footprint low relative volatility strong quarterly earnings acceleration recent up day volume exceeding prior 10 day maximum down day volume ready for pocket pivot breakout signal
ta_focus: LONG ONLY — do NOT recommend SHORT positions. POCKET PIVOT BUY — EXACT RULES from Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple (2010). (1) VOLUME SIGNATURE (the defining rule): On the pivot day, up-day volume must exceed the MAXIMUM down-day volume of the prior 10 trading sessions. This is the pocket pivot volume signature — earlier institutional accumulation signal than a standard base breakout. (2) BASE STRUCTURE: Stock must be in a constructive base of 3-15 weeks. Base should be tight (low volatility, ATR compressed), pulling back to and holding the rising 50-day MA. Avoid loose, wide bases. (3) LOCATION FILTER: Price must be within 0-5% ABOVE the 50-day MA on the pivot day (not extended). Also must NOT be more than 5% above the 10-day MA (avoid climax entries). (4) TREND FILTER: 50-day MA must be above the 200-day MA and rising. EMA stack aligned bullish. (5) CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: Only call BUY on the pocket pivot day CLOSE (when the up-day volume officially exceeds the 10-day down-day max) or next-day intraday within 2% of that pivot close. Do NOT front-run — the volume signature must be confirmed on the daily close. Before confirmation, use WATCH. (6) STOP-LOSS: 5-7% under the pivot day's low (tighter than CAN SLIM's 7-8% under pivot). Alternate: under the 50-day MA. (7) HOLDING RULES: Hold as long as price stays above the 10-day MA (short-term) or 21-day EMA (position). Exit into strength on 20% gain, or on close below the 21-day EMA. (8) DISQUALIFIERS: Skip pocket pivots when (a) stock is >5% extended above 10-day MA, (b) base is only 1-2 weeks old (too early), (c) RSI already >75 (extended), (d) volume signature is close to but not clearly above the 10-day down-day max. (9) QUALITY OVERLAY: Prefer stocks with CAN SLIM fundamentals — EPS acceleration, ROE 15%+, RS rank top quartile.
trading_style: Pocket pivot early-entry swing trader, 3-10 day holds getting into leaders on volume signature before base breakout, LONG ONLY

name: Bull Flag Continuation (Bulkowski)
description: LONG ONLY. Bull flag / high-and-tight flag continuation from Thomas Bulkowski's Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns, 2nd edition (2005) — the most comprehensive statistical study of chart patterns ever published. High-and-tight flag = 85% breakout success rate (Bulkowski's highest-rated pattern), reaching the measured target 70% of the time. Standard bull flag = 67% breakout success. Screens for a sharp pole (+20-50% in <=4 weeks) followed by a tight 3-7 day pullback flag retracing <=38.2% of the pole on declining volume.
screening_prompt: TSX stocks that just completed a sharp 20 to 50 percent price advance in 4 weeks or less followed by a tight 3 to 7 day pullback consolidation flag with declining volume forming continuation pattern near recent highs institutional buying footprint intact strong sector momentum uptrend clearly established EMA stack aligned bullish ready for flag breakout on volume expansion
ta_focus: LONG ONLY — do NOT recommend SHORT positions. BULL FLAG / HIGH-AND-TIGHT FLAG — EXACT RULES from Bulkowski Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns 2nd ed (2005). (1) POLE: A sharp, near-vertical price advance of +20% to +50% in 4 weeks or less. High-and-tight flag: +100% to +120% in 4-8 weeks. Volume must EXPAND during the pole (institutional buying). (2) FLAG PULLBACK: 3-7 day consolidation retracing NO MORE than 38.2% of the pole (Fibonacci). Ideal retracement 15-25%. Volume MUST decline through the flag (drying up — bulls holding). Flag should slope slightly against the trend (down for a bull flag). (3) FLAG DURATION: Standard bull flag 5-15 days ideal. High-and-tight flag 3-5 weeks tolerated. Flags longer than 15 days become pennants or rectangles — different patterns with lower win rates. (4) CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: Only call BUY after a daily candle CLOSES above the flag high on volume >= 1.5x flag-avg volume (surge confirms institutional re-entry). Before that close, use WATCH with the flag high as entry_price. (5) STOP-LOSS: Just under the flag LOW (mechanical). Aggressive: use the 21-day EMA if flag low is too far. (6) MEASURED TARGET: Pole length added to the breakout price. Example: pole from $10 to $15 (+50%), flag pullback to $13, breakout at $15 -> target = $15 + $5 = $20. (7) TRAILING STOP: Once price reaches 50% of the measured target, trail with the 21-day EMA. (8) TIME STOP: Exit if the flag breaks below its low without breaking to the upside — the continuation setup has failed. Also exit if price stalls at the breakout level for more than 3 days on rising volume. (9) DISQUALIFIERS: Skip if (a) pole rally was on declining volume (weak), (b) flag pullback exceeds 50% (too deep, becomes a base not a flag), (c) flag volume is HIGHER than pole volume (distribution not consolidation), (d) breakout attempt fails 2x in a row (pattern likely broken). (10) BEST WITHIN: Strong sector momentum, RS leaders, EMA 50 > 200, ADX >= 20.
trading_style: Bull flag continuation swing trader, 3-8 day holds targeting Bulkowski high-probability flag breakouts after a sharp pole, LONG ONLY
